# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system ("Old System") to the new billing system ("New System"). Both systems will run concurrently (dual-run) throughout the migration to allow reconciliation, fallback, and validation before any user's billing record is considered fully migrated. Decommissioning of the Old System is explicitly **out of scope** for this plan and must be handled as a separate, subsequent phase after the final migration batch has been validated and stable for an agreed soak period.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (Internal + Opt-In Volunteers)
**Population:** 1% of users (~400 users)
**Composition:** Internal employee accounts, test accounts, and a small pool of opt-in volunteer customers who have been briefed and given a support fast-lane.

**Entry criterion:**
- New System has passed a full end-to-end billing simulation (invoicing, proration, refunds, tax calculation, dunning) against a shadow copy of production data with zero critical discrepancies.
- Rollback procedure has been tested at least once in staging and completes in under 30 minutes.
- Dual-write/dual-read reconciliation tooling is live and generating diff reports at least every 4 hours.
- On-call and support teams have been briefed and runbooks are published.

**Exit criteria to advance to Phase 2:**
- No Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents attributable to the New System for 5 consecutive business days.
- Invoice/charge discrepancy rate between Old and New systems ≤ 0.1% of transactions.
- Support ticket volume for billing issues among canary users is not statistically elevated versus baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (Low-Risk Segments)
**Population:** 20% of users (~8,000 users), cumulative with Phase 1
**Composition:** Users on standard/simple billing plans (e.g., single-currency, no active disputes, no complex proration or multi-entity billing arrangements). Enterprise, high-ARR, and legally complex accounts are explicitly excluded from this phase.

**Entry criterion:**
- Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering Lead and Support Lead.
- Reconciliation diff rate from Phase 1 has remained ≤ 0.1% for the full 5-day observation window.
- Customer communication (email/in-app notice) has been sent to the Phase 2 cohort at least 7 days prior to migration, with an opt-out/delay mechanism for flagged accounts.
- Capacity review confirms New System infrastructure can handle 20x canary transaction volume with headroom (load test at 2x expected peak).

**Exit criteria to advance to Phase 3:**
- Cumulative discrepancy rate ≤ 0.1% across Phases 1–2 combined.
- Failed payment rate on New System is within 0.2 percentage points of the Old System's historical baseline for the same cohort.
- No unresolved Sev-1 incidents; Sev-2 mean time to resolution ≤ 24 hours.
- Finance sign-off on revenue reconciliation for the cohort (New System totals match Old System totals within agreed tolerance).

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Rollout (Remaining Users, in Batches)
**Population:** Remaining 79% of users (~31,600 users), migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., 4–6 sub-batches of ~13% each) rather than a single cutover, including complex/enterprise accounts last.
**Composition:** All remaining segments, sequenced from moderate complexity to highest complexity/highest ARR/legally sensitive accounts, with enterprise and high-touch accounts migrated only after a dedicated account-manager handoff call.

**Entry criterion:**
- Phase 2 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering Lead, Support Lead, and Finance.
- Dedicated migration runbook exists per remaining segment type (e.g., multi-currency, annual contracts, usage-based billing).
- Escalation path and dedicated war-room coverage staffed for the full duration of Phase 3.
- Each weekly sub-batch requires its own go/no-go review based on the prior sub-batch's metrics before proceeding — no sub-batch begins until the previous one has cleared the automatic halt thresholds below for at least 72 hours.

**Note on final batch:** The final sub-batch of Phase 3 completes user migration only. The Old System remains live, in dual-run/read-only reconciliation mode, for a minimum 30-day soak period after the final batch before any decommissioning discussion begins. Decommissioning the Old System is a separate, future initiative requiring its own approval, entry criteria, and rollback plan — it is not part of this rollout plan and will not occur within any phase defined here.

---

## Automatic Rollout Halt Thresholds (Metrics)

The rollout (i.e., starting any new batch/phase) must be **immediately halted** and escalated to the incident commander if, at any point:

- **Billing discrepancy rate** (New vs. Old system reconciliation diff) exceeds **0.5% of transactions** in any rolling 24-hour window.
- **Failed/declined payment rate** on the New System exceeds the Old System's trailing 30-day baseline by more than **1.5 percentage points** in any rolling 24-hour window.
- **Sev-1 billing incidents**: any single occurrence attributable to the New System halts the current phase pending root cause analysis.
- **Customer-reported billing complaints** exceed **150 tickets per 10,000 migrated users** in a rolling 7-day period.

A halt freezes migration of new users into the New System (already-migrated users remain, with Old System available as fallback) until root cause is identified, a fix is validated, and the Billing Engineering Lead and Support Lead jointly approve resumption.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missing charges during dual-run reconciliation causes customer billing disputes | Implement automated reconciliation jobs every 4 hours with alerting on any diff above threshold, and freeze migration of new batches until diffs are resolved | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: New System cannot handle peak transaction volume once majority of users are migrated, causing failed payments or timeouts | Run load tests at 2x projected peak volume before each phase, and maintain auto-scaling with capacity headroom validated ahead of Phase 3 | Infrastructure/SRE Lead
RISK: Complex enterprise accounts (multi-entity, custom contracts, non-standard tax rules) break in the New System due to edge cases not covered by simpler test cohorts | Sequence enterprise/high-complexity accounts last in Phase 3, require account-manager-led validation calls, and maintain per-segment runbooks | Enterprise Support Lead
RISK: Customers are not adequately informed of the migration and are confused by changes to invoices, payment methods, or billing portals | Send proactive email/in-app notifications at least 7 days before each user's migration with a support contact and opt-out/delay option | Customer Communications Lead
RISK: Data corruption or loss during account migration (e.g., stored payment methods, credit balances, coupon/discount states) | Run pre- and post-migration data integrity checksums per account and block advancement of any batch with unresolved integrity failures | Data Migration Engineering Lead
RISK: Rollback from New System back to Old System for an already-migrated user is slower or less reliable than expected during an incident | Test and time the rollback procedure before Phase 1 begins and after any major New System change, targeting under 30 minutes per account | Billing Engineering Lead

---

PHASES: 3
